newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to consolidate until weekend.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to consolidate until weekend.

text.p: The Belgian stock market paused on Thursday as investors took profits after recent record runs, but dealers said consolidation should be short-lived as more derivative products were expected to be launched on the market.
"We have been waiting for consolidation for weeks, this market needed a pause, we'll stay like this at least until the end of the week," said one trader.
By 0940 GMT the blue-chip Bel-20 was down 0.80 percent, or 17.70 points, at 2.192.91.
"We are still waiting for a few more derivative products to come onto the market, I know one bank has another 5 billion (Belgian francs) to place on the market," said another dealer.
The Bel-20 has recently benefitted from financial institutions launching derivative products or click funds, which lock in profits at certain Bel-20 index levels.
But dealers added that today's profit-taking was spurred on by Wall Street's overnight 46-point drop and sluggish bond markets.
Some dealers said investors were also worried over a possible U.S. interest rate hike.
Investors were also awaiting U.S. retail sales figures due at 1330 GMT, with the market expecting a 0.6 percent rise in February, according to a Reuter poll of economists.
Retail group GIB was the Bel-20's main loser, plunging 3.06 percent to 1,585 francs due to profit-taking.
Elsewhere oil and chemical group PetroFina fell 2.83 percent to 12,000 francs, with one dealer putting it down to a weaker dollar and softer oil prices.
"PetroFina for some reason is not liked by many investors, some say PetroFina's board does too little for its shareholders," said another trader.
Attention was also on companies about to release their 1996 results after the bourse close.
Insurer Royale Belge was down 0.12 percent at 8,530 francs.
Dealers said shares in Kredietbank were up 0.88 percent at 13,250 francs because the market expected good 1996 results.
Non-ferrous metals producer Union Miniere was down 1.48 percent at 2,670 francs. It will also release its 1996 results after the market closes.
